support.title: Have a question? We are here

description.one: If you have questions or want to learn more about my classes, reach out in any way that is convenient for you.

1.question: Is Frame Up suitable if I have never danced before?
1.answer: Yes, this style is perfect for beginners. We move step by step, paying attention to technique, body flow and confidence. The main thing is your desire to try and enjoy the process.

2.question: What should I bring to class?
2.answer: Wear comfortable clothes that let you move freely, bring socks or soft shoes, and a bottle of water. I will guide you through everything else on site.

3.question: Can I join in the middle of a month or course?
3.answer: Yes, you can start at any time. I will help you integrate quickly and catch up with the program.

4.question: Is Frame Up right for me if I feel shy or afraid to move?
4.answer: Frame Up helps you open up naturally. Classes are held in a safe atmosphere where every woman feels support and respect. Shyness usually fades after the first sessions.

5.question: What is the difference between offline and online classes?
5.answer: Offline gives you group energy, live emotions and personal corrections. Online gives flexibility, comfort at home and learning at your own pace. Both formats bring real results.

6.question: What skill levels are available?
6.answer: There are groups for beginners, intermediate dancers and students who want to go deeper into technique and performance. I will help you choose the right level.

7.question: Can I train if I am not flexible?
7.answer: Flexibility is a skill that can be developed. Frame Up gently helps you open your body, improve mobility and feel more feminine.

8.question: How do classes usually look?
8.answer: We warm up the body, study technique, work on body flow, posture and musicality, and then learn choreography. Every class is a mix of energy, emotion and creativity.

9.question: Can I attend a trial class?
9.answer: Yes, a trial class is available. It is the best way to feel the style and atmosphere and understand if this format is right for you. Registration is available here:

10.question: Is Frame Up suitable for any age?
10.answer: Absolutely. Frame Up is about femininity, confidence and joy of movement, not age limits.

1.title: Lesson 1: Footwork fundamentals
1.description: We start with the basics of foot placement, both in heels and without heels. You learn to feel support, distribute body weight and stay stable in every movement. This is the foundation of body flow and expression.

2.title: Lesson 2: Living body — waves and spine
2.description: We open the body to flow. You explore soft waves, spinal mobility and torso control. You learn to connect breath with movement so the dance feels alive, fluid and sensual.

3.title: Lesson 3: Legs — en l'air, swings, kicks
3.description: We develop leg strength and expression. You master core elements and learn to execute them technically, clearly and with character. We focus on lines, amplitude and control.

4.title: Lesson 4: Performance — gaze and emotion
4.description: Dance is not only technique, but also story. You learn to work with performance quality: gaze, facial expression and inner state. How to convey emotion, engage the viewer and feel confident on stage and in class.

5.title: Lesson 5: Putting it all into choreography
5.description: We combine everything you have learned into your first full choreography. You dance, feel and enjoy. This is the point where technique becomes art and movement becomes personal style.

hero.title: Frame Up
hero.subtitle: Discover yourself in Frame Up style
hero.description: Learn to dance beautifully, boldly and sensually in an atmosphere of freedom and feminine strength.

bio.1: I am Anna Strok, a professional dancer and teacher with many years of teaching experience and a clear artistic style.
bio.2: I am the creator and organizer of Total Strip Weekend in Minsk, the largest frame up strip and high heels championship in Belarus, which gathered hundreds of dancers and became an important event for the dance community.

quote.1: Today I develop Frame Up in Poland: I lead groups where women open up through movement, and I continue to learn from European masters to grow together with my students.
quote.2: My goal is to strengthen Frame Up culture and inspire women to be bold, free and expressive by creating a space where each woman can feel her strength, beauty and creative energy.

studio.title: Dancing in a studio feels completely different

paragraphs.1: In the studio you feel the energy of people around you, catch rhythm faster and open up with more confidence. Every movement becomes stronger when the group supports and inspires you.
paragraphs.2: Offline classes help you feel your body deeper, improve technique and get the emotional charge that online often misses. You do not just repeat movements - you live the dance.
paragraphs.3: Join studio classes and allow yourself more sensations, freedom and strength.

hero.title: Offline courses
hero.description: Everyone comes to Frame Up with a different story. Some wear heels for the first time, others already dance confidently and want to grow further. That is why classes are split by levels for comfortable progress without stress.

fromZero.title: Beginners
fromZero.description: Ideal if you are just starting. We focus on basic technique, body flow, posture, rhythm and confidence in movement.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: For dancers who strive for detail, dynamics and deeper style understanding, and want to improve musicality while working on technique, performance quality and memorizing more advanced choreographies.

impro.title: Impro room
impro.note: This group has no fixed schedule.
impro.details: Every month we decide when and where to meet, practice different exercises, explore details and nuances, and build our own dance language.

3.title: 3. Scope of collected data
3.text:
Collected data may include: first and last name, phone number, email address, usernames on social media platforms, as well as data necessary to process orders and communicate.
In the case of purchasing an online course, additional data may be processed: order-related data (course name, purchase date, payment status), technical and usage data (IP address, system logs), and — if applicable — data required for accounting documents (VAT ID / invoicing details).
As a rule, payment data is processed by the payment provider — the controller may only receive information about the payment status.

4.title: 4. Data recipients / processors
4.text:
Data may be transferred to entities supporting the controller in providing services, in particular:
- payment system providers (Stripe),
- hosting / course delivery platform (Telegram) / tools used to provide access to materials,
- email, communication, and customer support tools (Gmail),
- accounting services (if applicable),
- IT support.
Data is not sold or shared with third parties for their own marketing purposes. It may also be disclosed to public authorities only where required by law.

5.title: 5. Transfers of data outside the EEA
5.text: If you use providers based outside the European Economic Area (e.g., certain cloud services), personal data may be transferred outside the EEA only in accordance with the GDPR (e.g., based on Standard Contractual Clauses) and with appropriate safeguards in place.

6.title: 6. Data retention

7.title: 7. Rights of the data subject
7.text:
You have the right to access your data, rectify it, erase it, restrict processing, object to processing, data portability, and to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (PUODO).
Where processing is based on consent, you have the right to withdraw your consent at any time.

8.title: 8. Voluntary provision of data
8.text: Providing personal data is voluntary; however, it is necessary to participate in classes or events and to process an order for the online course and provide access to digital content.

9.title: 9. Automated decision-making / profiling
9.text: Personal data is not subject to automated decision-making or profiling.
